info.title: moonvalley/video-to-video-resize
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "moonvalley/video-to-video-resize", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for Moonvalley's video-to-video resize route: the video-to-video body plus optional frame position, frame resolution and scale 2-tuples.

example.prompt_text: Apply motion control to enhance this video

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for every Moonvalley route slug: the terminal `GET /proxy/moonvalley/prompts/{prompt_id}` prompt document, forwarded unchanged. All five operations are SUBMIT-AND-POLL against that ONE status route — the submit answers a prompt handle and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished prompt document rather than that handle.
The generated asset is at `output_url`, whatever the operation's medium: it is an image for `moonvalley/text-to-image` and a video for the other four. Comfy Router draws that line itself — a `completed` prompt carrying no `output_url` is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document — so through Router a `200` here always carries an asset URL. Fetch it; nothing is inlined in this body.
`status` is Moonvalley's own lowercase vocabulary. `completed` is the one terminal success. `error` is a terminal failure and reaches a Router caller as a Comfy Router error rather than as this document, with the provider's own detail under `error`. `queued` and `generating` are the in-flight states Router polls through and a caller never sees.
`inference_params`, `model_params`, `meta`, `frame_conditioning` and `error` are free-form objects Moonvalley does not document a shape for; they are forwarded as-is and this schema does not narrow them.

example.prompt_text: a single red maple leaf falling onto still water

MoonvalleyVideoToVideoRequest.description: Request body for Moonvalley's video-to-video prompt route. A control video and a control type are what distinguish this route from text-to-video, and Moonvalley requires both alongside the prompt.

example.prompt_text: Apply motion control to enhance this video
